Larkhollow rule — a revision is reconciled, not assumed. When a revision arrives, the reconciliation above runs again on what the revision says, against the curriculum vitae and against every verification already completed on the entries it touches. Dates are not the only thing a revision can move: the organization, the role, the supervisor and the verification contact all belong to the entry, and a change to any of them is a change to the entry. Section 11 says what re-opens when it does. The monitoring duty in section 11 runs alongside it and does not pause while a file waits.
3. The six checks
Six elements are verified in this procedure: licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. The manual numbers seventeen essential credentialing elements in Section 6, Subsection 4. Of the other eleven, nine are handled by the office outside this procedure, as stated above; current competency is the clinical leadership's, not the office's; and the manual's conditions-and-release form is replaced by our own Authorization and Release, which is part of intake in this procedure.
What counts as a verification at all
The manual, Section 1, defines primary source verification as
"Verifying a credential from the original source"
and Section 6, Subsection 1 rules out two things we see constantly:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
A reply that reached us through the applicant is not a verification, however genuine the document looks, however clear the letterhead, however real the registrar's signature. It goes in the file as received and the request stays open.
A designated equivalent source is acceptable in place of the original. The manual leaves each of its lists open — Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends
"etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications"
and element 5 ends
"or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications"
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied consistently, so ours is closed. The sources this office accepts for each element are named in attester-table.md. Anything not on that table is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional. It is never quietly accepted as good enough, and it is never quietly downgraded to a secondary source.
There is one legitimate route to a weaker source, and it opens only on impossibility. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 1:
"If completing primary or DES verifications is impossible, such as when an educational institution or residency program has closed, secondary source verifications may be used."
"When a primary or designated equivalent source cannot be obtained, the applicant's recent affiliations should be contacted to discover how they obtained the verification."
Larkhollow rule. Impossibility is a closed school, a closed programme, a dissolved employer — a source that no longer exists to answer. A source that exists and does not answer is not impossible; it is non-responsive, and non-response is handled in section 4, not here. When the secondary path opens, the reason is written into the file.
How often we ask, and what silence means
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 2:
"Verifications are attempted at least three times."
"Each attempt, including whom it was attempted to verify with, the date of request, verification methods, and any additional comments, is documented in the Notes section of the entry."
"Note that non-responsive individuals or entities may be a red flag."
And Section 15, on affiliations:
"If the affiliation is unwilling to complete the verification or is non-responsive after 3 attempts, this should be noted as a red flag."
Larkhollow rule. The attempt log is permanent. A reply arriving on the fourth attempt does not erase the three that went unanswered — the record of how hard the file was to verify is part of the file. Silence is never a pass. An unanswered request is an outstanding item for as long as it stays unanswered.
Check 1 — Licensure
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 6:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive professional medical licenses will be verified."
"Licenses will be verified before expiration."
and, on what a licence has to be:
"Every licensed practitioner who provides patient care in federal facilities must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States."
Larkhollow rule — the practice state. The manual's sentence above is a federal facility's rule: it accepts a licence from any State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or a territory, and Section 15 says so again, answering the question "Where is it documented that a practitioner does not need to be licensed in the state where they provide services in a federal facility?" with
"Federal law at 25 U.S.C. § 1621t states that licensed health professionals employed by a tribal health program are exempt if licensed in any state, from the licensure requirements of the state where services under an ISDEAA agreement are performed."
We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us. Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.
Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
Larkhollow rule — where the five years are measured from. The manual states the window and not its anchor. Ours is the date the application was first received: an entry is inside the window when any part of it falls in the five years counted back from the date the application was first received. A later revision does not move the anchor.
Element 4 defines a gap and says what is owed:
"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"
"Verification of time gaps is not required, but an explanation is."
Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.
Judgment
	Whose
	Whether a gap explanation is satisfactory
	Clinical Director
	Whether a finding is disqualifying
	Clinical Director, then the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and the Governing Body
	Whether to discontinue an application on eligibility grounds
	Clinical Director
	Whether to recommend appointment, and which privileges
	Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
	Whether to grant, modify, defer or deny
	Governing Body
	The office's job on each is to present the evidence the decider needs and to record the disposition that comes back. Presenting well is the work; deciding is not.
7. The Medical Services Professional's own role
The manual, Section 4, states it:
"verify, analyze, and prepare all relevant information regarding an LP's competency, character, training, experience, and judgment to present a complete and accurate file to the MEC and GB for recommendations and approvals"
8. Packet readiness
The manual, Section 12:
"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
9. The committee protocol
The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
and the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
"proposes a recommendation through the clinical director (CD) and the chief executive officer (CEO) or their designee to the Governing Body"
Section 7:
"The GB or a delegated GB committee retains the final authority to grant, renew, or deny privileges after considering the recommendations of the medical staff"
Section 12, on who may record what:
"All signatories should utilize a "recommend" selection, with only the Chair of the GB or their designee using the "approval" selection."
A recommendation is not an approval. A record from the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff that carries the word "approved" is still a recommendation, because those bodies cannot approve. Only the Governing Body chair, or the designee named in authority-roster.md, records an approval.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible. All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
1. the body is one that may record that outcome;
2. the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
3. the decision names the same applicant and the same application revision as the presentable packet;
4. a presentable packet existed for that revision before the decision date;
5. the outcome is one of approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, not recommended, and every outcome other than a plain approval carries a reason.
A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision. It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision. A second decision for the same application revision is admissible only when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision. recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
Larkhollow rule — deferral. A deferral names the information it waits for. The office chases exactly that, and the file does not advance while it waits.
10. Activation and the appointment cycle
The manual, Section 5:
"The provider cannot provide patient care services until the practitioner has been approved for their next appointment and privilege cycle."
and Section 15:
"The GB needs to approve a provider's privileges and/or appointment on or before the"
expiry date, to prevent a lapse; and a later start date is permitted when the body records it:
"Yes, if the GB makes the notation in their final notes when they sign off on the signature pages in Virtual Committee."
Larkhollow rule — activation. On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates exactly the privilege groups named in the decision — never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.
Larkhollow rule — approve with conditions. An approval with conditions activates the approved privilege groups on the normal rule above, and records each condition as a monitored condition with its own due date. A condition is satisfied only by a record naming it. A condition still unmet on its due date becomes a finding to the Clinical Director.
Monitored conditions do not block activation. A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
The manual, Section 15:
"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
"must continue monitoring expirables even during the review process and always provide the most current information"
A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.
Larkhollow rule — the five re-entry triggers, and what each affects:
What arrives
	What it affects
	A new application revision
	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
	A credential expires or is renewed
	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.","id":"REDACTED","parent_ids":null,"drive_id":null,"created_time":"2026-09-24T07:01:51.663Z","modified_time":"2026-09-24T07:01:52.694Z","is_empty":false,"mime_type":"text/plain","file_name":null,"file_size_bytes":null,"url":"https://drive.google.com/file/d/REDACTED"}},"isError":false}

﻿Professional peer reference — blank request and return form
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-REF-2026.1.
The office sends this form directly to the referee the applicant named, and the referee returns it directly to the office. A form that reaches us through the applicant cannot be used.
________________
Part 1 — completed by the Medical Staff Office before sending
Field
	Content
	Referee identifier
	The office's identifier for this referee on this file
	Applicant
	Name and degree
	Privileges requested
	The privilege groups on the application
	Request date
	The date this request was sent
	Request number
	1, 2 or 3 — each reminder is a fresh numbered request
	We write up to three times, 21 calendar days apart. If no reply has reached us by the 64th day after the first request, we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open. We do not close it as satisfied and we do not count it.
________________
Part 2 — completed by the referee
Field
	What to enter
	Are you a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant?
	Tick Yes or No. This box is never left blank
	Relationship
	How you worked with the applicant, in your own words
	Your specialty
	The clinical discipline you practise, chosen from the same list the applicant chose from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery — or your own discipline if it is not on that list
	Dates you worked directly together
	First and last date. Leave the last date blank only if you still work together
	Recommendation
	Recommend without reservation, Recommend, Recommend with reservations, or Do not recommend
	Comments
	Character, clinical experience, competency, and anything else you want on the record
	Signature and signature date
	The date you sign. This is the date we measure currency from — not the date we receive the form
	Who may give a peer reference
Three conditions, each independent, all three required:
1. you have worked directly with the applicant within the two years ending on the day you sign this form;
2. you practise in the same clinical discipline as the applicant;
3. you are not a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant.
If any one of the three does not hold, say so on the form and return it anyway. We will record your reply, and we will not count it towards the two references the appointment needs. That is not a judgment about you or about the applicant; it is the rule we apply to every file the same way.
Currency
A reference is current if the signature date is within two years of the date the file is presented to the Governing Body. A reference signed a long time before the file is presented stops being current, and we ask again.
________________
Part 3 — completed by the Medical Staff Office on return
Field
	Content
	Received date
	The date the completed form reached the office
	How it arrived
	Secure portal, letter, fax or email, direct from the referee
	Nothing in Part 2 is edited, summarized or corrected by the office. What the referee wrote is what goes in the file, including a relationship or a specialty that differs from what the applicant told us.

﻿Accepted sources by element — who may attest
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Table version LARK-ATT-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
The manual we adopted leaves its source lists open. Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends "etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications", and element 5 ends "or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications".
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied the same way twice, so ours is closed. This table is the whole list. A reply from a source on it is admissible. A reply from any source not on it is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional — it is not quietly accepted, and it is not quietly treated as a secondary source.
Two rules cut across every row, both the manual's, both from Section 6, Subsection 1:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
So the applicant is never an accepted source for any element, on any row below, however genuine the document they carry. The reply is filed as received and the request stays open.
Education and training
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The degree-granting school's registrar's office or dean's office. The sponsoring institution's graduate medical education office or programme director, for a residency or fellowship
	Designated equivalent source
	Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG). Federation Credentials Verification Service of the Federation of State Medical Boards (FCVS). American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. National Student Clearinghouse
	Secondary source — only on impossibility
	The applicant's most recent affiliation's medical staff office, stating how it obtained its own verification, when the school or programme has closed and no designated equivalent source holds the record. The reason is written into the file
	Not accepted
	The applicant. An alumni association. A departmental colleague writing in a personal capacity. A recruiter, staffing agency or locum tenens agency. A photocopied or scanned certificate from any hand
	Licensure
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The issuing state licensing board, through its own online verification service or a written reply from the board
	Designated equivalent source
	Federation of State Medical Boards Physician Data Center
	Secondary source
	None. A state licensing board does not close
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A prior employer's copy of a licence. An aggregator or directory not named above
	Board certification
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The issuing certifying board, through its own verification service or a written reply
	Designated equivalent source
	American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) certification verification. CertiFACTS. American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. American Board of Physician Specialties (ABPS). American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA)
	Secondary source
	None
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A certificate image. A specialty society membership roster
	Affiliations and employment
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The affiliated hospital's medical staff office. The employer's human resources department or the practice's authorized administrator
	Designated equivalent source
	A credentials verification organization retained by that affiliation or employer, where the reply names the organization and the affiliation it acted for
	Secondary source — only on impossibility
	Where the employer has dissolved and no successor holds the records, a written account from the applicant's most recent surviving affiliation of what that affiliation verified, with the reason written into the file
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A supervisor writing from a personal address without the employer's authority. A professional networking profile. A letter of recommendation offered in place of a dates-and-position verification
	What to do with a reply that is not on this table
1. Record it as received, with who sent it and how it arrived. Nothing is discarded.
2. Mark the entry still outstanding. An inadmissible reply does not resolve anything.
3. Keep requesting from a source that is on the table, and keep logging each attempt.
4. Raise it to the Medical Services Professional, who decides whether the case is one of the impossibility routes above.
Non-response is not impossibility. A source that exists and does not answer is a non-responsive source: it stays outstanding, the attempts keep being logged, and the manual's red flag applies. Only a source that no longer exists opens the secondary route.

﻿How this office exports its credentialing records
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office A note from the Medical Services Professional to whoever automates the initial-appointment file. Written 2026-03-16, alongside the first export.
I run the export from the credentialing database every few weeks and drop it in the shared folder, one sub-folder per export. Here is what you get, what the columns mean, and the three or four things that catch people out.
The export date is the clock
Every batch folder has a README.md that says the export date and the window it covers. That date is the clock for everything in the folder: nothing in a batch happened after its export date. Work the batch as if today were the export date. Do not use the real date you run your tool, and do not carry today's date into an arithmetic that a batch is supposed to settle.
The three exports are 2026-03-16, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-18. The first one covers everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The second and third cover only what changed since the previous one.
The caseload at an export date is every application file the office has received up to that date, however that file ended. A withdrawn or discontinued file stays in the caseload with its final status; a later batch never removes a file, it only adds to what is known about it.
A batch is closed. It never changes.
I never go back and edit an export. If an applicant corrects something, a new revision of the application appears in a later batch and the old one stays exactly where it was. If a board sends a corrected reply, the corrected reply is a new row and the old row stays. If a committee decides something twice, there are two decision records.
So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.
The files
Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
File
	One row is
	applications.csv
	an application revision I received in the window
	application-disclosures.csv
	one professional practice question and the applicant's answer
	declared-history.csv
	one history entry the applicant declared
	declared-credentials.csv
	one licence or certification as the applicant described it
	privilege-requests.csv
	one privilege group requested
	licence-lookup-wa.csv
	one Washington credential record from the state board's lookup
	licence-lookup-other-states.csv
	one out-of-state credential record
	certification-replies.csv
	one certifying board's reply
	verification-replies.csv
	one reply about education and training, or about an affiliation or employer
	verification-attempts.csv
	one request I sent
	peer-referees.csv
	one referee named on an application, or supplied later
	peer-reference-replies.csv
	one completed reference form that came back
	correspondence.csv
	one letter, memo or decision record, with the path to the document
	

Folder
	What is in it
	letters/
	applicants' explanation letters, withdrawals, referee substitutions, and my own written requests for missing items
	dispositions/
	the Clinical Director's recorded dispositions
	decisions/
	Credentials Committee and Executive Committee minutes extracts, and Governing Body approval records
	correspondence.csv is an index. It tells you the documents exist and where they are. It does not tell you what they say — you have to open them.
A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.
Dates, blanks and columns
* Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Always. A date range is inclusive at both ends: an entry from_date 2022-01-01, to_date 2022-12-31 covers the 1st of January and the 31st of December. An expiry date is the last day the credential is valid.
* An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean "no", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:
   * a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;
   * a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.
* No money appears anywhere. We do not record fees, salaries or contract values in the credentialing file.
* Files are UTF-8 with Unix line endings. Values are quoted only when they contain a comma.
The three joins that matter
1. Everything on the applicant side joins on application_id, and on revision where the fact belongs to a revision. Entries, credentials, privilege requests and disclosures all restate on each revision, so always filter to the revision you are working.
2. The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.
3. A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.
The Washington export's own columns
I pass that file through as the board publishes it and add one column. The board's twelve are credentialnumber, credentialtype, status, firstissuedate, lastissuedate, expirationdate, ceduedate, actiontaken, birthyear, firstname, middlename, lastname. Mine is lookup_date — the day I ran the lookup. It is my own act, not a source's reply, so the usability window is not applied to it.
Two of the board's columns are easy to misread:
* ceduedate is a continuing-education due date. We do not use it. Continuing education is handled outside this procedure and it has nothing to do with whether a licence is valid.
* actiontaken says the board has acted. It does not say what the action was. For that you need the board's written reply, which arrives as a document, not in this file. A Yes here is a reason to go and read; it is not a conclusion.
The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.
How often anything is actually wrong
I want to say this plainly, because a small sample of credentialing files can leave the wrong impression.
In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.
The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.
The clean files are genuinely clean. If your tool raises something on one of them, it is your tool.
What I do not export
My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.
Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.

content.text: I found implementation assumptions that exceed the sources: requiring a new verification request after every changed entry, and requiring both a name and email for every history entry. Neither explains the current batch-wide holds. The pre-dispatch status gap still stands independently. I also found that “Partial” is being reported without the snapshot that REQUIREMENTS.md requires for a consumed partial batch.

I found implementation assumptions that exceed the sources: requiring a new verification request after every changed entry, and requiring both a name and email for every history entry. Neither explains the current batch-wide holds. The pre-dispatch status gap still stands independently. I also found that “Partial” is being reported without the snapshot that REQUIREMENTS.md requires for a consumed partial batch.

**G1 has a genuine contract gap, alongside implementation assumptions that should be corrected.** I could not find an existing status that truthfully represents the documented pre-dispatch hold. The missing-evidence holds are substantially justified, but they must describe facts **not established by the export**, rather than defects proved against all 40 applicants.

I read the requirements, complete schema, E-5 interview, six office sources and representative batch records before evaluating the tracker and troubleshooting reports. All six source captures match the linked originals after line-ending normalization. All 29 batch-1 files match their capture hashes, and all 13 CSV tables match retained working history.

**1. No existing status covers the pre-dispatch intake hold truthfully.**

The [schema’s status definition](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/snapshot.schema.json:162) rules out the plausible alternatives:

| Candidate | Why it does not fit |
|---|---|
| `intake-incomplete` | Requires an item already requested in writing and a running applicant clock. |
| `returned-incomplete` | Asserts that the file was returned. |
| `ineligible-clock-expired` | Requires an expired response clock. |
| `in-verification` | Requires a complete file. |
| `deferred` | Requires an admitted Governing Body deferral; it is not a generic waiting status. |
| `decision-inadmissible` | Does not cover files without refused decisions, and cannot bypass the schema’s intake precedence. |
| Null, omission, or a new status | Violates the required status enumeration. |

The interview explicitly requires holding the file and recording **pending dispatch**, with the response clock starting subsequently. It supplies no alternative status or permission to reinterpret the schema. [E-5, 22:44](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/interviews/interview-E-5.md:880)

APP-2026-001 demonstrates the gap without depending on the implementation: its application row supplies release and CV receipt dates but no application-signature evidence; its only indexed correspondence is an inbound recommendation, not an applicant intake request. [Application](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/applications.csv:2), [correspondence](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/correspondence.csv:10)

**The exact contradiction:** every application must appear in the snapshot with a permitted status; required intake completeness is unestablished; no request, return, expiry or terminal event supports an intake status; and the interview forbids advancement or inventing dispatch. These obligations cannot all be satisfied under the unchanged status definition. An action-queue explanation cannot cancel a false status assertion. [Snapshot requirements](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/REQUIREMENTS.md:50)

**2. The evidence holds are mostly justified, but their scope needs precise wording.**

| Evidence requirement | Independent assessment |
|---|---|
| Application signature and date | **Outstanding for all 40 on the supplied evidence.** The procedure separately requires application and release signatures. `release_signed_date` cannot establish both. This does not prove that any application was actually unsigned. [Procedure §1](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:20) |
| CV presence | **Established for 39; missing for APP-019.** Those 39 should not receive a missing-CV intake finding merely because the CV contents were not exported. The interview defines currentness through presence, without an additional age test. [Applications](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/applications.csv:1), [E-5, 20:50](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/interviews/interview-E-5.md:750) |
| CV reconciliation | **Outstanding across the supplied batch.** Receipt dates cannot perform the required comparison with application and verified evidence. An unavailable CV also cannot establish a discrepancy. [Procedure §2](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:35) |
| School and qualifying training accreditation | **Legitimate missing facts.** Accredited education and training are explicit criteria. APP-001’s accepted registrar/GME replies verify its degree, specialty and dates, but do not establish accreditation. Its residency duration is already exactly 36 months. [Criteria](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/privilege-criteria.md:6), [APP-001 replies](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/verification-replies.csv:2) |
| Direct peer return | **Outstanding provenance, distinct from eligibility.** The batch contains 57 peer replies, but their fields do not establish the return route. A request’s portal method does not prove how the response arrived. The form explicitly excludes applicant-routed returns. [Reply fields](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/peer-reference-replies.csv:1), [form](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/peer-reference-form.md:3) |
| Referee addresses | **Not an export hold.** The export note expressly excludes this check and requires it to remain neither met nor failed. [Export exception](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/export-note.md:77) |

I considered the strongest contrary evidence: the export note says clean files are genuinely clean, and APP-001’s committee minute says the file was presented. Neither identifies the missing facts. The later interview question expressly names signatures, CV reconciliation, accreditation and direct referee responses; Renata says missing required evidence remains outstanding. Treating the broad “clean files” statement as proof would override that specific answer. [Export note](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/export-note.md:74), [minute](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/decisions/2026-03-10_MEC-2026-011.md:19), [E-5, 21:33](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/interviews/interview-E-5.md:840)

The resulting eligibility questions also have explicit support: criteria rule 6 requires referral while nothing yet verified supports a requested group, and permits withdrawal of the question when later verification establishes support. They are **not findings that all 40 applicants lack qualifications**, nor authority to discontinue them. [Criteria rule 6](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/privilege-criteria.md:79)

My independent count confirms 40 applications, 41 revisions, 38 null working statuses and two supported intake statuses: APP-019 has its documented March 20 deadline; APP-018 was actually returned incomplete. [APP-019 letter](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/letters/2026-02-18_missing-items_APP-2026-019.md:8), [APP-018 letter](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/letters/2026-03-06_return-incomplete_APP-2026-018.md:8)

**3. Some implementation choices exceed the authoritative requirements.**

- **Missing evidence is hardcoded rather than assessed conditionally.** Signature and CV-reconciliation holds are appended unconditionally; accreditation and peer provenance are always unverified. These conclusions fit the inspected evidence, but the code would not clear them merely because adequate evidence became available. That is a reusable-processing limitation, not proof that today’s holds are wrong. [Intake logic](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/engine.py:134), [accreditation logic](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/evidence.py:174), [peer logic](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/evidence.py:259)

- **A changed entry automatically requires a newly dated verification request.** The code rejects earlier-request replies solely because their request predates the revision. The office instead requires reconciliation against existing verifications and entry-specific assessment of what changed. A fresh request may be necessary, but its date is not a universal admissibility condition. This rule did not account for the current batch-wide holds. [Implementation](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/evidence.py:127), [procedure §2](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:45), [usability rule](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:178)

- **Contact completeness is broader than specified.** The code requires both contact name and email for every history entry. The intake rule requires a verification contact for employers and affiliations; it does not prescribe email or extend that intake condition to every school/training entry. No current batch-1 hold arose from this overreach. [Implementation](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/engine.py:161), [source rule](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:28)

- **“Partial” without a snapshot does not satisfy the contracted Partial outcome.** The implementation deliberately emits that combination. REQUIREMENTS.md requires unsettled applications to remain in the snapshot. The current artifacts are useful diagnostic working results, but G1 remains blocked at snapshot production. [Implementation](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/io.py:370), [run outcomes](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/REQUIREMENTS.md:39)

**The smallest defensible resolution is one explicit contract clarification**, broadening the existing `intake-incomplete` description to cover completeness not yet established before dispatch:

> Before a written request is recorded, hold the file and queue MSP dispatch; no applicant response clock has started. After dispatch, apply the recorded request date and response deadline.

The existing action queue can carry the distinction, with `due: null` unless a record fixes a date. No new enum or additional snapshot fields are necessary. This changes the status’s permitted meaning and therefore needs contract-owner review; it cannot be presented as an interpretation already authorized by the current wording.

That clarification would remove the snapshot-representation blocker while preserving every legitimate evidence hold. The implementation overreach above should be corrected separately; none supplies a defensible shortcut to readiness.

No files were modified, no credentialing run was executed, and no implementation was begun. Stopped for your review.

| CV presence | **Established for 39; missing for APP-019.** Those 39 should not receive a missing-CV intake finding merely because the CV contents were not exported. The interview defines currentness through presence, without an additional age test. [Applications](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/applications.csv:1), [E-5, 20:50](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/interviews/interview-E-5.md:750) |

[Criteria](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/privilege-criteria.md:6), [APP-001 replies](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/verification-replies.csv:2) |

[Reply fields](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/inputs/batch-01/peer-reference-replies.csv:1), [form](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/peer-reference-form.md:3) |

[Implementation](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/evidence.py:127), [procedure §2](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:45), [usability rule](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:178)

[Implementation](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/engine.py:161), [source rule](/home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/sources/procedure.md:28)

+# Independent G1 review
+
+Review date: 2026-10-21. Scope: independently assess the G1 blocker against the original requirements, complete snapshot schema, office sources linked in interview E-5, the interview itself, and representative batch records before evaluating the tracker and troubleshooting conclusions.
+
+This document records the completed read-only review. Recommendations are proposals for owner review, not implemented changes or authorization to change the contract. No implementation, requirements, schema, source records, or working results were modified during the review. No credentialing run was executed.
+
+## Conclusion
+
+**G1 has a genuine contract gap, alongside implementation assumptions that should be corrected.** I could not find an existing status that truthfully represents the documented pre-dispatch hold. The missing-evidence holds are substantially justified, but they must describe facts **not established by the export**, rather than defects proved against all 40 applicants.
+
+The smallest defensible resolution is an explicit contract clarification broadening the existing `intake-incomplete` description to cover the pre-dispatch phase. That would allow unresolved evidence and owned work to be represented without inventing dispatch, deadlines, verification, or approval. The implementation assumptions identified below require separate corrections; they do not explain away the current status gap.
+
+## Evidence and review method
+
+I read [REQUIREMENTS.md](../REQUIREMENTS.md), the complete [snapshot.schema.json](../snapshot.schema.json), [interview-E-5.md](../interviews/interview-E-5.md), all six linked office sources, and representative batch-1 records before evaluating the [project tracker](../PROJECT-TRACKER.md), [G1 troubleshooting report](g1-troubleshooting.md), [APP-001 evidence trace](g1-evidence-trace.md), and [Q07 compatibility report](g1-q07.md).
+
+The six office sources were checked against their linked native Google Docs using the Google Drive skill and read-only connector calls:
+
+| Local capture | Linked original |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Procedure](../sources/procedure.md) | [LARK-MSO-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+| [Accepted-source table](../sources/attester-table.md) | [LARK-ATT-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+| [Privilege criteria](../sources/privilege-criteria.md) | [LARK-PRIV-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+| [Authority roster](../sources/authority-roster.md) | [LARK-AUTH-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+| [Export note](../sources/export-note.md) | [Office export note, 2026-03-16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+| [Peer-reference form](../sources/peer-reference-form.md) | [LARK-REF-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
+
+All six captures matched the linked originals after line-ending normalization and trimming of boundary whitespace. Their local hashes also matched the source manifest. All 29 batch-1 files matched their capture hashes, and all 13 CSV tables matched the raw tables retained in working history. These comparisons establish capture/retention consistency; they do not prove that unexported documents do not exist in the office.
+
+Representative records included APP-2026-001's application, history, verification replies and attempts, peer records, certification, correspondence, and committee recommendation; APP-2026-019's missing-items notice and intake data; APP-2026-018's return-incomplete notice and history; APP-2026-031's licence correspondence; and the written gap explanations for APP-2026-005 and APP-2026-039. Counts and retained-state comparisons were computed with independent standard-library scripts, without running the credentialing implementation.
+
+## 1. Existing statuses do not truthfully cover the pre-dispatch intake hold
+
+The [schema's status definition](../snapshot.schema.json) at line 162 rules out the plausible alternatives:
+
+| Candidate | Why it does not fit |
+| --- | --- |
+| `intake-incomplete` | Requires an item already requested in writing and a running applicant clock. |
+| `returned-incomplete` | Asserts that the file was returned. |
+| `ineligible-clock-expired` | Requires an expired response clock. |
+| `in-verification` | Requires a complete file. |
+| `deferred` | Requires an admitted Governing Body deferral; it is not a generic waiting status. |
+| `decision-inadmissible` | Does not cover files without refused decisions, and cannot bypass the schema's intake precedence. |
+| Null, omission, or a new status | Violates the required status enumeration. |
+
+The remaining statuses require readiness, approval, activation, denial, withdrawal, or discontinuation facts that do not establish a general pre-dispatch intake hold.
+
+The interview explicitly requires holding the file and recording **pending dispatch**, with the response clock starting subsequently. It supplies no alternative status or permission to reinterpret the schema. See [E-5, Renata at 22:44](../interviews/interview-E-5.md), lines 880–884.
+
+APP-2026-001 demonstrates the gap without depending on the implementation: its [application row](../inputs/batch-01/applications.csv), line 2, supplies release and CV receipt dates but no application-signature evidence; its only [indexed correspondence](../inputs/batch-01/correspondence.csv), line 10, is an inbound recommendation, not an applicant intake request.
+
+**The exact contradiction:** every application must appear in the snapshot with a permitted status; required intake completeness is unestablished; no request, return, expiry or terminal event supports an intake status; and the interview forbids advancement or inventing dispatch. These obligations cannot all be satisfied under the unchanged status definition. An action-queue explanation cannot cancel a false status assertion. See [REQUIREMENTS.md, Snapshot contract](../REQUIREMENTS.md), lines 50–54, and the schema's required application fields and status definition, lines 139–178.
+
+Substituting `intake-incomplete` would satisfy the mechanical enum check but contradict its stated meaning. The schema's intake-precedence sentence does not establish that dispatch occurred. Likewise, the broad business meaning of “Deferred” in the run outcomes does not broaden the narrower application-status enum.
+
+## 2. Missing-evidence holds are mostly justified, with important distinctions
+
+| Evidence requirement | Independent assessment |
+| --- | --- |
+| Application signature and date | **Outstanding for all 40 on the supplied evidence.** [Procedure §1](../sources/procedure.md), lines 20–22, separately requires application and release signatures. `release_signed_date` cannot establish both. This does not prove that any application was actually unsigned. |
+| CV presence | **Established for 39; missing for APP-019.** Those 39 should not receive a missing-CV intake finding merely because the CV contents were not exported. The interview defines currentness through presence, without an additional age test. See [applications.csv](../inputs/batch-01/applications.csv) and [E-5, Renata at 20:50](../interviews/interview-E-5.md), line 750. |
+| CV reconciliation | **Outstanding across the supplied batch.** Receipt dates cannot perform the required comparison with application and verified evidence. An unavailable CV also cannot establish a discrepancy. See [procedure §2](../sources/procedure.md), lines 35–45. |
+| School and qualifying training accreditation | **Legitimate missing facts.** Accredited education and training are explicit criteria. APP-001's accepted registrar/GME replies verify its degree, specialty and dates, but do not establish accreditation. Its residency duration is already exactly 36 months. See [criteria](../sources/privilege-criteria.md), lines 6 and 15, and [APP-001 replies](../inputs/batch-01/verification-replies.csv), lines 2–3. |
+| Direct peer return | **Outstanding provenance, distinct from eligibility.** The raw batch contains 57 peer replies, but their fields do not establish the return route. A request's portal method does not prove how the response arrived. The form explicitly excludes applicant-routed returns. See [reply fields](../inputs/batch-01/peer-reference-replies.csv), line 1; [APP-001 requests](../inputs/batch-01/verification-attempts.csv), lines 6–7; and [peer form](../sources/peer-reference-form.md), lines 3 and 46–53. Files without replies have a separate missing-response problem; the 57-row total is not a count of currently qualifying replies. |
+| Referee addresses | **Not an export hold.** The export note expressly excludes this check and requires it to remain neither met nor failed. See [export exception](../sources/export-note.md), line 77. |
+
+I considered the strongest contrary evidence: the [export note](../sources/export-note.md), line 74, says clean files are genuinely clean, and [APP-001's committee minute](../inputs/batch-01/decisions/2026-03-10_MEC-2026-011.md), line 19, says the file was presented. Neither identifies the missing facts. The later interview question expressly names signatures, CV reconciliation, accreditation and direct referee responses; Renata says missing required evidence remains outstanding. Treating the broad “clean files” statement as proof would override that specific answer. See [E-5, 21:33](../interviews/interview-E-5.md), lines 840–844.
+
+An accepted source and an established fact are different questions. A registrar/GME reply can be admissible and establish the degree or training dates without establishing accreditation. Similarly, a peer reply can establish discipline, relationship, direct work and signature currency without establishing direct return. These established facts must remain retained; missing provenance is not proof of an inadmissible route, and missing accreditation evidence is not proof of an unaccredited programme.
+
+The resulting eligibility questions also have explicit support: [criteria rule 6](../sources/privilege-criteria.md), line 79, requires referral while nothing yet verified supports a requested group, and permits withdrawal of the question when later verification establishes support. They are **not findings that all 40 applicants lack qualifications**, nor authority to discontinue them.
+
+Independent counts and retained-output inspection confirmed:
+
+- 40 applications and 41 application revisions.
+- Release and CV receipt dates recorded for 39 current application revisions.
+- Application-signature evidence listed as outstanding for all 40 current assessments; CV reconciliation also outstanding for all 40.
+- 38 null working statuses and two supported intake statuses.
+- Zero presentable packets in the retained results.
+
+The two represented intake files are grounded in actual events. APP-019 has its documented March 20 deadline from the February 18 request for release and CV; APP-018 was actually returned incomplete and has an April 5 response deadline. See the [APP-019 letter](../inputs/batch-01/letters/2026-02-18_missing-items_APP-2026-019.md), line 8, and [APP-018 letter](../inputs/batch-01/letters/2026-03-06_return-incomplete_APP-2026-018.md), line 8. APP-019's existing letter does not establish that signature evidence or two named referees were also requested.
+
+The APP-001 recommendation cannot supply missing underlying evidence or independently establish prior readiness. Refusing it for unestablished prior presentability remains defensible under [procedure §9](../sources/procedure.md), lines 194–200. A recommendation is not Governing Body approval.
+
+## 3. Implementation assumptions exceeding the sources
+
+### Missing evidence is hardcoded rather than assessed conditionally
+
+Signature and CV-reconciliation holds are appended unconditionally; accreditation and peer provenance are always unverified. These conclusions fit the inspected evidence, but the code would not clear them merely because adequate evidence became available. That is a reusable-processing limitation, not proof that today's holds are wrong.
+
+Code references:
+
+- [engine.py](../credentialing/engine.py), lines 134–138: application-signature evidence is always appended to the missing list.
+- [engine.py](../credentialing/engine.py), line 195: CV-reconciliation work is always appended.
+- [evidence.py](../credentialing/evidence.py), lines 115–118 and 174–176: accreditation is initialized unverified and every education entry receives a missing-accreditation issue.
+- [evidence.py](../credentialing/evidence.py), lines 259–265: every peer return receives missing-provenance and unusable results.
+
+**Recommended correction:** make these evidence-dependent checks with traceable resolution when sufficient supplied evidence exists. Preserve today's holds until such evidence is actually available. The rules require facts to be established; they do not require permanent failure because a particular CSV lacks a dedicated column. This also follows the reusable Skill requirement in [REQUIREMENTS.md](../REQUIREMENTS.md), line 69.
+
+### Changed entries automatically require a newly dated verification request
+
+The code rejects earlier-request replies solely because their request predates the revision. The office instead requires reconciliation against existing verifications and entry-specific assessment of what changed. A fresh request may be necessary, but its date is not a universal admissibility condition.
+
+References: [evidence.py](../credentialing/evidence.py), lines 127–145; [procedure §2](../sources/procedure.md), line 45; and the [usability rule](../sources/procedure.md), line 178. The latter explicitly says a later revision does not by itself void completed verifications and requires entry-by-entry evaluation.
+
+**Recommended correction:** assess whether retained verification establishes the revised entry's relevant facts. Require fresh verification for facts not established, rather than using request date alone as a universal rejection rule. No current batch-1 assessment had this revision-mapping restriction applied, so it did not account for the batch-wide holds.
+
+### Contact completeness is broader than specified
+
+The code requires both contact name and email for every history entry. The intake rule requires a verification contact for employers and affiliations; it does not prescribe email or extend that intake condition to every school/training entry.
+
+References: [engine.py](../credentialing/engine.py), lines 161–166, versus [procedure §1](../sources/procedure.md), line 28.
+
+**Recommended correction:** scope the intake condition to the stated entry types and accept the contact information the authoritative rules actually require. Missing information needed to perform a particular verification can still generate owned verification work without inventing a broader intake rule. No current batch-1 hold arose from this overreach: the inspected entries all had both fields.
+
+### “Partial” without a snapshot does not satisfy the contracted Partial outcome
+
+The implementation deliberately emits `Partial` with no snapshot when statuses are unrepresentable. [REQUIREMENTS.md, Run outcomes](../REQUIREMENTS.md), lines 39–46, requires unsettled applications to remain in the snapshot. The current artifacts are useful diagnostic working results, but G1 remains blocked at snapshot production.
+
+References: [io.py](../credentialing/io.py), lines 370–398, sets `Partial`, retains `snapshot: null`, and writes a snapshot only when no status is unrepresented. The [tracker](../PROJECT-TRACKER.md), lines 364–369, and [troubleshooting report](g1-troubleshooting.md), line 46, describe these working results as Partial while acknowledging the missing public snapshot.
+
+**Recommended correction:** distinguish “diagnostic working results retained” from a contract-complete Partial batch result. Report G1's snapshot-production blocker explicitly; do not imply that retaining working files fulfills the required snapshot obligation. Evidence holds alone need not be run failures once they can be represented truthfully.
+
+## Smallest defensible resolution for owner review
+
+**One explicit contract clarification** would remove the representation blocker: broaden the existing `intake-incomplete` description to cover required intake completeness not yet established before dispatch. Proposed meaning:
+
+> intake-incomplete — required intake completeness is not established. Before a written request is recorded, hold the file and queue MSP dispatch; no applicant response clock has started. After dispatch, apply the recorded request date and response deadline.
+
+The existing action queue can carry the distinction, with `due: null` unless a record fixes a date. Existing documented requests retain their actual deadlines and coverage. No new enum or additional snapshot fields are necessary.
+
+This changes the status's permitted meaning and therefore needs contract-owner review; it cannot be presented as an interpretation already authorized by the current wording. If the contract remains unchanged, no complete truthful batch-1 snapshot can be claimed from the inspected evidence. Substituting `in-verification`, a generic `deferred`, fabricated dispatch, or an invented status is not a defensible workaround.
+
+After an authorized clarification, the proposed implementation correction is narrow: project the pre-dispatch hold using the clarified status while retaining the owned dispatch action, unknown deadline, evidence deficits, refusal history, and lack of approval/activation. Separately correct the evidence-handling and rule overreach identified above. Those corrections must not mark the present missing facts verified or manufacture readiness.
+
+This agrees with the previous troubleshooting conclusion on the narrow Q07 incompatibility, but does not accept its implementation as free of unsupported assumptions. It also distinguishes the genuine missing-evidence problem from the snapshot-representation problem: obtaining every missing business fact is not necessary merely to represent unresolved work once the contract can express it.
+
+## Limits and stop point
+
+This review independently inspected batch-1 records and current working outputs; it did not process batches 2 or 3, rerun the credentialing CLI or test suite, or independently inspect the full IHS manual. Published-manual authority here is limited to quotations adopted in the supplied office sources. Local hash agreement is not an independent remote checksum for every batch file.
+
+No files were modified during the original review, and no implementation was begun. This document is the sole file created by the subsequent instruction to save the review. All recommended contract and implementation changes remain unimplemented and await owner review.
*** End Patch"));

| [Procedure](../sources/procedure.md) | [LARK-MSO-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
| [Accepted-source table](../sources/attester-table.md) | [LARK-ATT-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
| [Privilege criteria](../sources/privilege-criteria.md) | [LARK-PRIV-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
| [Authority roster](../sources/authority-roster.md) | [LARK-AUTH-2026.1](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
| [Export note](../sources/export-note.md) | [Office export note, 2026-03-16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit) |
